title: Volume and surface area
lede: Volume is how much a box holds; surface area is how much cardboard it takes. Prisms, cylinders, cones and spheres.

sections.md:
## Volume = base × height
For any **prism** or **cylinder** (same shape all the way up), volume is the area of the base times the height.

| Solid | Volume |
|---|---|
| Rectangular box | l × w × h |
| Cube | s³ |
| Cylinder | πr²h |
| Triangular prism | (½bh of triangle) × length |

Units are **cubed**: in³, m³.

## Pointy shapes are one third
A **cone** or **pyramid** holds exactly **one third** of the prism or cylinder with the same base and height.

- Cone: V = ⅓πr²h
- Pyramid: V = ⅓ × base area × h
- Sphere: V = ⁴⁄₃πr³

## Surface area
Surface area is the total area of all the faces, the wrapping paper. Units are **squared**.

- **Box:** 2(lw + lh + wh), three pairs of matching rectangles.
- **Cylinder:** 2πr² (top and bottom) + 2πrh (the label, unrolled into a rectangle).

sections.label: Scaling again
sections.md: Scale every length by k: surface area scales by k², volume by **k³**. Double the size of a box and it holds 8 times as much.
